forks.title: A Western defence scheme for the Middle East
forks.text: The Western powers invite Israel to join a proposed Middle East defence organisation in which Egypt would be a founder. The cabinet must decide how to answer, and the Knesset is divided between those who want closer ties with the West and the left, which wants no alliance with either bloc.

options.label: Stay open to the scheme, but only after peace with the Arab states
options.advocate: Ben-Gurion

cite.quote: it was indicated by Premier David Ben Gurion when he conferred with American Ambassador Monnet B. Davis this week

options.note: Ben-Gurion told the US ambassador that Israel could join only after an Arab-Israeli peace.

lasting.label: Door left open to the Western powers
Left-wing opposition to a Western orientation
Western aid and credit stay on offer

options.label: Decline to take part in any Western-led alliance
options.advocate: Mapam (Jacob Riftin)

cite.quote: Mapam’s Jacob Riftin took the floor to criticize the Middle East command

lasting.label: Left-wing parties back a non-aligned line
Seen as outside the Western camp

forks.title: National service for religious women
forks.text: Religious women are exempt from army service on grounds of conscience. The government proposes two years of non-military national service for them, in immigrant camps, schools and clinics, with exemption committees. The Agudah and other religious circles protest.

options.label: Introduce two years of national service for religiously exempt women
options.advocate: Labour Minister Golda Myerson and the government

cite.quote: it was the intent of the government to increase the available labor power by drafting Orthodox young women who were unable to serve in the Army for religious or family reasons for other jobs

options.note: The bill passed its first reading 59-6 in July 1953 and became the National Service Law of 1953; by 1978 it was reported frozen for coalition reasons (S5016).

lasting.label: Extra labour for immigrant camps, schools and clinics

options.label: Keep the exemption and do not draft religious women
options.advocate: Agudah (Rabbi I. M. Lewin)

lasting.label: Religious public keeps faith in the coalition
Religious parties stay in the coalition

forks.title: Egypt's arms from the Soviet bloc
forks.text: Egypt announces a large arms purchase from Czechoslovakia. Israel protests in Prague and Moscow and must choose a response: buy arms wherever it can to keep the balance, or put its weight behind a request for Western arms and a formal security pact.

options.label: Acquire the arms needed to keep a balance with Egypt, wherever they can be bought
options.advocate: The cabinet and the Knesset

cite.quote: The Israel Cabinet decided today to acquire whatever arms are needed to maintain a balance of armaments with Egypt

options.note: On 4 October 1955 the cabinet decided to acquire whatever arms were needed; the Knesset backed it almost unanimously on 25 October.

lasting.label: Arms balance with Egypt kept

options.label: Make a Western arms supply and a formal security pact the main demand
options.advocate: US Representative Hugh Scott

cite.quote: a security pact to batten down the status quo in the Middle East, were called for in a statement sent to Secretary of State John Foster Dulles this week-end by Rep. Hugh Scott

lasting.label: Closer commitment from the Western powers sought

forks.title: Which partners for the government?
forks.text: Mapai governs with the religious parties as its partners and calls the arrangement unstable. The centrist General Zionists will join if economic controls are scrapped and the party school 'trends' are merged into one state system, which the religious parties oppose. Whom does the cabinet bring in?

options.label: Bring the General Zionists in, scrap most economic controls and merge the school trends
options.advocate: Mapai leadership and the General Zionist Party

cite.quote: Economic controls shall be scrapped, except on materials which cannot be produced in the country.
Apparently the religious parties will be the only ones to suffer if the centrists enter the government

options.note: Mapai and the General Zionists signed a coalition agreement on 17 December 1952 to run to the end of the Knesset term, scrapping most controls and merging the school trends (S5101).

lasting.label: Economic controls scrapped, private enterprise freed
Price and currency stabilisation drive
One state school system

options.label: Keep the religious parties as partners; leave the controls and school trends as they are

cite.quote: the religious parties will lose their fight against the amalgamation of the four “trend” schools into one state system

lasting.label: Religious parties stay in the government

forks.title: The Jordan canal and the aid cut
forks.text: Israel is digging a canal at Bnot Yaakov in the demilitarised zone on the Syrian frontier to divert Jordan water. The UN truce chief orders it halted, Syria goes to the Security Council and the United States suspends economic aid of about $65 million a year. Does Israel keep digging or suspend the work?

options.label: Suspend the canal work and let the Security Council examine the water question
options.advocate: US Secretary of State Dulles and the UN truce supervision chief

cite.quote: agreed that the work started by Israel in the demilitarized zone would be suspended pending urgent examination of the question by the Council
The United States has officially notified Israel that economic assistance for the Jewish State is being suspended

options.note: Israel agreed in the Security Council to suspend the work and the United States resumed aid (S5104). The Carrier later drew water from the Sea of Galilee instead.

lasting.label: Cooperation with the Security Council over the canal
US grant of about $26 million resumed
Jordan diversion delayed until the Carrier
US aid and trade ties preserved
US technical cooperation continues

Negev settlers wait for water

options.label: Keep digging the canal in the demilitarised zone
options.advocate: The Israeli Cabinet and chief water engineer Simcha Blass

cite.quote: The decision to continue work on the project was taken at a meeting yesterday of the Israel Cabinet.
Simcha Blass, Israel’s chief water planning engineer

lasting.label: Jordan water diverted earlier
Public rallies behind the water project

forks.title: Who runs the Defence Ministry?
forks.text: Defence Minister Pinhas Lavon has resigned after Prime Minister Sharett refused his proposals for changes in the defence set-up. Ben-Gurion, in retirement at Sde Boker, is asked by Mapai colleagues to return. Border raids and the Egyptian arms question press on the cabinet.

options.label: Call Ben-Gurion back as Defence Minister
options.advocate: Prime Minister Moshe Sharett and Mapai's leaders

cite.quote: I felt convinced that no candidate would have the prospect of discharging the tasks more successfully

options.note: Ben-Gurion was confirmed by the Knesset 74 to 22 on 22 February 1955 (S5106).

options.label: Give the Defence Ministry to a figure agreed with all the coalition partners
options.advocate: General Zionist papers Haaretz and Haboker, and the Mizrachi paper Hatzofeh

cite.quote: These papers charged that no consideration had been given to the fact that Israel is governed by a coalition
Sharett's alleged failure to consult Mapai's partners in the Cabinet came under heavy fire from Haaretz and Haboker, General Zionist organs, and from Hatzofeh, the Mizrachi paper.

forks.title: Arms from Bonn and a cabinet in crisis
forks.text: Ben-Gurion wants to send a senior envoy to West Germany to negotiate arms purchases. Ahdut HaAvoda leaked the cabinet decision and, with Mapam, objects both to dealing with Germany and to his demands for cabinet secrecy and discipline. The coalition may break.

options.label: Pursue the arms talks with Bonn and rebuild the coalition on secrecy and collective responsibility
options.advocate: Prime Minister David Ben-Gurion

cite.quote: Ben Gurion wanted to send to West Germany to negotiate the purchase of arms
Ministers bind themselves to preserve complete secrecy in matters of security and foreign policy

options.note: Ben-Gurion resigned, then presented a reconstituted five-party coalition with secrecy and collective-responsibility rules on 8 January 1958 (S5108).

lasting.label: Arms supply from West Germany
German credit and trade

forks.title: Who is registered as a Jew?
forks.text: Interior Minister Israel Bar-Yehuda of Mapam has issued population registry rules under which a person can be entered as a Jew on his own declaration that he belongs to no other religion. The rules set off a world-wide 'Who is a Jew?' controversy. Should the registry follow personal declaration or the religious-law definition?

options.label: Register as Jews only those with a Jewish mother or who convert
options.advocate: Interior Minister Moshe Shapira and the religious parties

cite.quote: only persons with a Jewish mother or persons who undergo religious conversion may be registered as Jews

options.note: In January 1960 Shapira cancelled Bar-Yehuda's rules and restored the mother-or-conversion rule (S5109).

lasting.label: Religious partners stay in the government

forks.title: The Johnson plan for the refugees
forks.text: Joseph Johnson, envoy of the UN Palestine Conciliation Commission, proposes that each Palestinian refugee choose return, resettlement in Arab countries or elsewhere. Israel would keep a security veto over individuals and pay indemnities. The Arab states reject any plan that mentions resettlement.

options.label: Reject the plan: Israel alone decides who is admitted
options.advocate: Foreign Minister Golda Meir

cite.quote: Mrs. Golda Meir, Israel’s Foreign Minister, rejected the plan on behalf of her Government

options.note: Meir rejected the plan for Israel and the Arab states rejected it as well, and it was not carried out (S5113).

lasting.label: Israel seen to block the Johnson plan
Relatives of Arab citizens remain refugees

lasting.label: A serious compensation offer

forks.title: German scientists in Egypt
forks.text: German scientists and technicians are helping Egypt develop missiles. After the arrest of two men in Basle on charges of threatening a scientist, the cabinet must set a line toward Bonn, which supplies arms and aid.

options.label: Demand that Bonn legislate, through the Foreign Ministry and a Knesset resolution, while keeping the arms and aid ties

options.note: The Knesset passed a unanimous resolution on 20 March 1963; in July the Foreign Minister rejected opposition calls for a further general debate (S5115, S5117).

forks.title: Answering the plan to divert the Jordan headwaters
forks.text: The Arab summit in Cairo has decided to divert the Jordan headwaters and set up a joint military command, while Israel prepares to draw water from the Sea of Galilee within the Johnston plan quotas. How should Israel respond if the diversion works go ahead?

options.advocate: Chief of Staff Yitzhak Rabin

options.note: By July 1965 the army had twice hit Syrian equipment used for diversion work (S5120).

forks.title: A constitution now, later or never?
forks.text: The Knesset must decide whether Israel should have a written constitution. Mapai, the Sephardim, the Progressives and WIZO propose building one gradually out of basic laws; the Religious Bloc would postpone the drafting indefinitely; Mapam and 37 members from several parties want a constitution drafted at once. The vote is in mid-June 1950.

options.label: Build a constitution gradually, out of basic laws passed one at a time
options.advocate: Mapai, the Sephardim, the Progressives and WIZO

cite.quote: a compromise offered by the Mapai, Sephardim, Progressives and WIZO

options.note: On 13 June 1950 the Knesset voted 50 to 0, with 13 abstentions, to work out basic legislation that would gradually be built into a constitution (S5400).

lasting.label: Religious and secular parties both accept the compromise

options.label: Draft a full written constitution at once

options.advocate: The Religious Bloc

cite.quote: The Religious Bloc had supported a proposal that the drafting of a Constitution be postponed indefinitely

forks.title: Korea: take a side at the UN?
forks.text: North Korea has attacked the South and the UN Security Council has called for aid to South Korea. Israel's declared policy is non-identification with either bloc. The cabinet has backed the resolution; Mapam, Herut and the Communists attack the decision in a tense Knesset debate.

options.label: Support the Security Council resolution and the UN action in Korea
options.advocate: Foreign Minister Moshe Sharett and Prime Minister David Ben-Gurion

options.note: The Knesset upheld the cabinet's support for the resolution by 68 to 20, with 8 abstentions, on 5 July 1950 (S5402).

forks.title: Test the Suez Canal blockade?
forks.text: After the withdrawal from Sinai, Egypt still bars Israeli ships and cargo from the Suez Canal and has issued its own declaration on the canal. Delegations friendly to Israel at the UN advise testing Egypt with a ship or at least Israeli cargo; the United States and France are being consulted, and Israel is against taking the question to the Hague Court.

options.advocate: Prime Minister David Ben-Gurion and the Foreign Ministry

options.note: No Israeli ship was sent. Israeli cargo in foreign ships was held up at the canal in 1959 (S5407, S5408), and the first Israeli-flag vessel transited in May 1979 (S5409).

forks.text: Finance Minister Levi Eshkol plans to devalue the pound from 1.8 to 3 to the dollar on 9 February, freeze prices and leave the next cost-of-living allowance until the July adjustment. Ahdut HaAvoda and Mapam want workers' allowances raised at once and relief for farmers whose loans are linked to the dollar.
